summary:
Advisory Marswalk route planner that audits orbital evidence, stress-tests segments, and projects crew resources with a turn-back clock.
Cairn: Trail Mode is a hackathon planning aid for a small Mars traverse area (Jezero Crater and Gale Crater). Crews draw waypoints on a map, calculate routes, and review evidence-backed segment verdicts (Terrain, Current conditions, Thermal), resource margins, stress-test outcomes, and a printable mission brief. It clearly distinguishes measured/cached/placeholder data and is advisory only—not flight-certified and without live telemetry.
details:
The challenge

Planning a safe EVA/traverse on Mars requires combining terrain, imagery coverage, environmental context, and resource constraints. Data can be incomplete, coarse, outdated, or unavailable, and crews need a clear way to understand what evidence supports each route segment, where uncertainty remains, and when to turn back.

What it does

Interactive route planning: Draw/edit waypoints on a 2D map for selected regions (Jezero/Gale), calculate mission routes, and inspect per-segment dossiers.

Evidence auditing (3 claim types): Runs Terrain/bedrock, Current surface conditions, and Thermal context audits in one calculation; users can switch claim views without recalculating.

Verdicts & explainability: Segment-level verdicts (Supported/Check/Fragile), flags/checks, coverage/scale/value-type context, and “needed observation” guidance.

Stress testing: Scenarios such as unseen obstacle and slope error to evaluate route robustness and update verdicts/resource projections.

Resource & safety projections: Derived estimates for oxygen, power, time/daylight margins, turn-back clock/point, mission verdict, and hard-stop/fix guidance (based on editable, unvalidated assumptions).

Map visualization: USGS basemap (reloads for visible extent where available), slope overlay, instrument footprints (CTX/HiRISE/CRISM/THEMIS), route/alternate/stops/comms layers, 2D/3D terrain view when DEM + WebGL are available (3D is visual aid, not used in audit; HiRISE detail where local data exists).

Crew support views: Visor mode for stepwise/text (and speech when available) route guidance; Brief view for a print-ready/save-as-PDF mission evidence brief with sources, caveats, margins, and stress results.

Context tools: NASA rover context image lookup (labeled not exact route location), registry/gaps info, project save/load (browser), configurable assumptions/parameters.

Live crew tracker (added on rofeat): Share/drop a crew member’s position on the planning map by callsign, view live/last-seen markers and movement history trails so others can see where someone was last seen (map-coordinate based, session-backed API; not Earth GPS/live telemetry).

How it works / architecture

Frontend: React + Vite + Leaflet (2D) + Three.js (3D terrain), served as static build or via Vite dev server (proxies /api to backend).

Backend: Python FastAPI (backend.app.main:app) providing APIs for status/layers/basemap, DEM/HiRISE terrain assets, footprints/registry, routing, evidence dossiers, stress tests, resources/mission/brief generation, params, NASA context endpoints, and crew tracker endpoints.

Data handling: Prefers live NASA/USGS/PDS-ODE sources where available; supports local demo cache/prep for offline-ish demos. Clearly labels placeholder/synthetic fallback data and unavailable sources; does not fabricate DEM/basemap when uncached retrieval fails.

Routing:DEM/grid-based route planning with slope constraints and cost weighting; segment audits combine footprint coverage, scale/type/age checks, and configured assumptions to produce verdicts, flags, and recommendations.
